name: Shelomith
title: The Woman Whose Son Blasphemed God's Name
summary: Shelomith was an Israelite woman from the tribe of Dan, daughter of Dibri. She is known from Leviticus where her son, who had an Egyptian father, blasphemed and cursed God's name in the camp, leading God to give Moses the law concerning punishment for blasphemy.

keyEvents.title: Shelomith's Origin
keyEvents.description: Shelomith is identified as the daughter of Dibri from the tribe of Dan, an Israelite woman who had a son with an Egyptian man.

keyEvents.title: The Son's Conflict in the Camp
keyEvents.description: Shelomith's son got into a dispute with an Israelite man in the camp, and during the conflict he blasphemed and cursed the Lord's name.

keyEvents.title: The Son Is Brought Before Moses
keyEvents.description: The blasphemous son was brought before Moses and held in custody until the Lord's will was made known.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on Blasphemy
keyEvents.description: The Lord spoke to Moses and commanded that all who heard the blasphemy should lay their hands on the guilty person's head, and the whole congregation should stone him.

keyEvents.title: Execution of the Judgment
keyEvents.description: The Israelites took the son of Shelomith outside the camp and stoned him, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. This set a precedent for how blasphemy should be handled.

keyEvents.title: The Law on Blasphemy Is Established
keyEvents.description: The incident with the son of Shelomith led God to establish a general law that anyone who curses the name of the Lord must die, whether they are a native or a foreigner.
